agyos_skill.instructions: The **transparency content type** — find the true moment inside the business, sharpen its specifics and stakes, check what's safe to reveal, and frame it in the founder's own voice. The **format writers** turn it into cuts, **WoopSocial publishes**, and the **human owns what gets revealed** — forever. Brand pages talk; founders get followed. Founder-voice content reliably out-engages the same message from a logo (personal profiles out-reach company pages by a wide margin; audiences say founder/employee voices are more credible than brand voices — see the reality file). But the mechanism isn't "being personal" — it's **specificity + stakes + honesty**. A real number ("we lost our biggest client, 31% of MRR"), a real decision ("we killed the feature 60% of users asked for — here's why"), a real process (the messy v1 next to the launch shot). Two counterfeits fail: **manufactured vulnerability** (the cried-in-my-car post engineered for reach — audiences smell it, and it's the defining cringe of the genre) and the **humble-brag** (a "mistake" that's secretly a trophy: "my flaw is I care too much"). And transparency has a hard edge: the internet is permanent, so what you reveal about customers, teammates, and legal matters is a one-way door. The skill is finding the genuinely interesting true thing, and knowing where the curtain stays down. 1. **brand-profile** — what the business actually is, holds, and has lived through. 2. **voice-builder** — the founder's real voice (and where the brand account's voice differs). (Depth: `references/the-reveal-framework.md`.) - **R — Root it in what actually happened:** this week's real work, decision, mistake, or milestone — surfaced, never invented; if it didn't happen, it isn't BTS. - **E — Expose the specifics + stakes:** the number, the tradeoff, the cost; "we shipped v2" is a press release, "we rewrote checkout twice and refunded 43 orders" is behind the scenes. - **V — Vet the transparency tier:** share (process, decisions, lessons, resolved mistakes) · handle with care (revenue, ongoing struggles, pricing logic) · **never** (customer data, team conflicts/personnel, legal, security). The human owns the reveal; it's permanent. - **E — Establish whose voice:** founder-voice (first person, owns "I", posts from the personal account) vs brand-voice (curates "we"); don't ghost-write feelings the founder doesn't have.
